hints: A move removes one coin from any nonempty selection of heaps.
Look only at heap parities: removing from every odd heap makes all heaps even.
If all heaps are even, any move creates at least one odd heap.
analogy: The first player can make every heap even; after that, mirror the opponent's parity changes.
example: For heaps [2,2], all are even, so the first player must make at least one odd; the second can restore evenness and win.
algorithm: If every heap has even size, print second; if any heap is odd, print first. A winning first move removes one from each odd heap.
correctness: From an all-even state every move makes some heaps odd. From a state with odd heaps, removing one coin from all odd heaps creates an all-even state. Thus the second player can mirror this response until the first player has no move.
complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space per test case.
